alg-thick-and-implicitly-restarted-arnol:
## Definition

Let $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, let $v\ne0$, and choose integers
$1\le r<m\le n$, a residual tolerance $\tau\ge0$, a restart budget
$N_{\max}\ge1$, a target rule, and a restart mode `thick` or `implicit`.
All operations below are in exact arithmetic. In thick mode, the target rule
selects $r-k$ linearly independent current Ritz vectors, where $k$ denotes
the number of already locked pairs; if it cannot do so, the procedure returns
`rank-loss`. In implicit
mode, a shift rule supplies exactly $p=m-r$ complex shifts for the current
cycle, or reports that the shift list is unavailable. The shifts may be chosen
from unwanted Ritz values, but the procedure allows any supplied list and
asserts no convergence for an arbitrary schedule. Initialize the restart
counter $c=0$ before the first Arnoldi cycle. A cycle consists of expanding
the current Arnoldi basis to dimension $m$ or exact breakdown, then computing
Ritz pairs and testing their original residuals. After the initial cycle in
step 1, each restart in step 3 or 4 constructs the next cycle. The output is
the locked Ritz pairs, the current unlocked Ritz pairs, and one of `converged`,
`budget-exhausted`, `invariant-subspace-breakdown`, `rank-loss`,
`shift-count-unavailable`, or `filtered-breakdown`.

1. Start with $v_1=v/\|v\|_2$, no locked pairs, and run fully reorthogonalized
   Arnoldi to dimension $m$, stopping earlier if the next Arnoldi residual is
   zero. Normalize every nonzero projected eigenvector $y$ so $\|y\|_2=1$ and
   lift it to $u=V_my$. For each Ritz pair $(\theta,u)$, compute the original
   residual $r_u=Au-\theta u$ (on a standard Arnoldi cycle it may be evaluated
   by [[prop-ritz-residual-formula-for-an-arnoldi-ritz-pair]]) and accept the
   pair when $\|r_u\|_2\le\tau$. Accepted pairs are recorded as locked outputs
   and their vectors must be retained at every later restart. If at least $r$
   pairs have been accepted, return `converged`.

2. If the projected Arnoldi space is exactly invariant and fewer than $r$ pairs
   have been accepted, return `invariant-subspace-breakdown`. If the restart
   counter satisfies $c=N_{\max}$, return `budget-exhausted`.

3. For a thick restart, form a target block from every locked vector and the
   additional wanted Ritz vectors selected by the target rule. Apply exact
   exact column-pivoted QR as in
   [[def-full-reduced-and-column-pivoted-computational-qr-factorisations]] to
   this block; if its rank is too small to retain all
   locked and selected directions, return `rank-loss`. With the resulting
   orthonormal basis $U$, compute the residual block
   $R_U=(I-UU^*)AU$. Apply exact column-pivoted QR as in
   [[def-full-reduced-and-column-pivoted-computational-qr-factorisations]] to
   $R_U$, breaking pivot
   ties by original column order, to obtain an ordered orthonormal basis $F$ of
   its range. If $U$ has $q$ columns, retain only the first
   $\min(\dim\operatorname{range}(R_U),m-q)$ columns of $F$, so $[U,F]$ has at
   most $m$ columns. Restart from $[U,F]$ and extend by block Arnoldi, fully
   reorthogonalizing each new $Aq$ against all current columns, until the basis
   has dimension $m$ or the exact residual vanishes. If the retained subspace
   is invariant before dimension $m$ and fewer than $r$ pairs are accepted,
   return `invariant-subspace-breakdown`.

4. For an implicit restart, use this branch only when no pair is locked. Set
   $p=m-r$ and request a shift list $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_p$ from the shift rule;
   if it reports a list of the wrong length, return `shift-count-unavailable`.
   Starting from $AV_m=V_mH_m+\beta_m v_{m+1}e_m^*$, apply exact shifted QR
   steps to $H_m$ using the Givens transformations of
   [[def-real-and-complex-givens-transformations]] in top-down adjacent-row
   eliminations on pairs
   $(1,2),(2,3),\ldots,(m-1,m)$:
   $H_{j-1}-\mu_jI=Q_jR_j$ and $H_j=Q_j^*H_{j-1}Q_j=R_jQ_j+\mu_jI$.
   Put $Q=Q_1\cdots Q_p$, rotate $V_m$ by $Q$, retain its first $r$ columns,
   and continue Arnoldi to dimension $m$. If the polynomial
   $q(z)=\prod_{j=1}^p(z-\mu_j)$ annihilates the starting vector or the
   filtered Krylov space has dimension below $r$, return `filtered-breakdown`.

5. Increment the restart counter by setting $c\gets c+1$, recompute Ritz
   pairs and their original residuals, apply the acceptance rule in step 1,
   and return to step 2 unless a return status applies.
   No convergence is asserted for an arbitrary shift schedule. The residual
   acceptance test certifies only the computed residual size; it does not by
   itself give a forward eigenvalue bound for a nonnormal matrix.
thm-implicit-restart-polynomial-subspace:
## Statement

Let $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, and suppose an exact $m$-step Arnoldi
factorization without breakdown is
$$AV_m=V_mH_m+\beta_m v_{m+1}e_m^*,\qquad V_m^*V_m=I_m,$$
where $H_m$ is upper Hessenberg and $\beta_m>0$. Let $1\le r<m$,
$p=m-r$, and let $H_{j-1}-\mu_jI=Q_jR_j$ be exact shifted QR factorizations
using the ordered top-down adjacent-row Givens eliminations on pairs
$(1,2),(2,3),\ldots,(m-1,m)$, with $R_j$ upper triangular. Put
$$Q=Q_1\cdots Q_p,\qquad H^+=Q^*H_mQ,\qquad q(z)=\prod_{j=1}^p(z-\mu_j).$$
Assume $q(A)v_1\ne0$, the exact filtered Krylov space
$K_r(A,q(A)v_1)$ has dimension $r$, and $\rho\ne0$ in the factorization
$q(H_m)=QR$ with $R$ upper triangular. Then
$$\operatorname{range}(V_mQ(:,1:r))=K_r(A,q(A)v_1).$$
Writing $H_r^+=H^+(1:r,1:r)$, $h^+=H^+_{r+1,r}$, and
$$g=h^+V_mQe_{r+1}+\beta_m(e_m^*Qe_r)v_{m+1},$$
the truncated restart has the exact residual identity
$$AV_mQ(:,1:r)=V_mQ(:,1:r)H_r^++g e_r^*.$$
If $g\ne0$, then $v_{r+1}^+=g/\|g\|_2$ is orthogonal to the retained
columns and the new Arnoldi residual coefficient is $\beta_r^+=\|g\|_2$;
if $g=0$, the retained subspace is exactly invariant.
alg-block-lobpcg-with-rank-loss-status:
## Definition

Let $A=A^*\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, let $B=B^*>0$, and let
$T=T^*>0$ be a fixed preconditioning operator. Here $B>0$ and $T>0$ mean
$x^*Bx>0$ and $x^*Tx>0$ for every nonzero $x$. The $B$-inner product and
norm are those of [[def-b-inner-product-and-dual-norm-for-definite-pencil]].
Choose a block width $1\le q\le n$, a residual tolerance $\tau\ge0$, a finite
iteration budget $N_{\max}\ge0$, and an initial matrix $X_0$ with
$X_0^*BX_0=I_q$. The output is a block of Ritz pairs and one of
`converged`, `budget-exhausted`, `rank-loss`, or `invalid-initial-block`.

1. If $X_0$ does not have full column rank or does not satisfy
   $X_0^*BX_0=I_q$, return `invalid-initial-block`. Compute the Rayleigh-Ritz eigenpairs in
   $\operatorname{range}(X_0)$, sorted increasingly, and let $\Theta_0$ be the
   diagonal matrix of the $q$ Ritz values. Set the previous search block
   $D_0$ empty and initialize the iteration counter $k=0$.

2. At iteration $k$, form the original residual block
   $R_k=AX_k-BX_k\Theta_k$. If every column has Euclidean norm at most
   $\tau$, return `converged`. If $k=N_{\max}$, return
   `budget-exhausted` with $(\Theta_k,X_k)$.

3. Compute the preconditioned residual block $W_k=TR_k$ and set
   $Y_k=[X_k,W_k,D_k]$, omitting the empty block at $k=0$. Compute an exact
   rank-revealing $B$-QR with column pivoting as follows. Starting with no
   columns in $Q_k$, for each remaining column $y_j$ of $Y_k$ compute its
   residual $c_j=y_j-Q_k(Q_k^*By_j)$ and choose a column with largest
   $B$-norm $\|c_j\|_B$ (break ties by original column order). If the largest
   residual norm is zero, stop; otherwise append the normalized residual to
   $Q_k$ and remove that pivot column. Let $s_k$ be the number of columns
   appended and let $\Pi_k$ record the pivot order followed by the unused
   columns. If $s_k<q$, return `rank-loss` with the current Ritz pairs; no
   projected solve is attempted on that branch. Otherwise set
   $$S_k=Q_k^*BY_k\Pi_k(:,1:s_k).$$
   The pivot construction gives
   $$Y_k\Pi_k(:,1:s_k)=Q_kS_k,\qquad Q_k^*BQ_k=I_{s_k},$$
   and $S_k$ is invertible because its selected columns are independent.
   Dependent trial columns are discarded and their count is recorded as a
   rank-compression diagnostic.

4. The projected matrix $Q_k^*AQ_k$ is Hermitian, hence normal, so its
   orthonormal eigenbasis and real eigenvalues are supplied by
   [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]. Solve
   $Q_k^*AQ_kZ_k=Z_k\Theta_{k+1}$ and choose its $q$ smallest eigenvalues. Set
   $C_k=\Pi_k(:,1:s_k)S_k^{-1}Z_k$; then $Y_kC_k=Q_kZ_k$. Partition
   $C_k=\begin{bmatrix}C_X\\C_W\\C_D\end{bmatrix}$, omitting the $C_D$
   block when $D_k$ is empty. The projected metric is positive definite
   because for nonzero $z$, $(Q_kz)^*B(Q_kz)=\|z\|_2^2>0$. Set
   $$X_{k+1}=X_kC_X+W_kC_W+D_kC_D,\qquad D_{k+1}=W_kC_W+D_kC_D,$$
   again omitting the empty-block term. Let $\Theta_{k+1}$ be the selected
   diagonal Ritz-value matrix and increment $k$.

5. Repeat from step 2. No convergence, rate, or accuracy is asserted when the
   budget or rank-loss branch is returned. The exact SPD conditions on $B$ and
   $T$ define the permitted metric and preconditioner; no particular
   incomplete-factorization procedure is assumed.
thm-finite-budget-restarted-and-block-pr:
## Statement

Consider any execution of [[alg-thick-and-implicitly-restarted-arnoldi-with-locking]]
or [[alg-block-lobpcg-with-rank-loss-status]] on inputs satisfying that
procedure's stated hypotheses. Assume every invoked target or shift rule,
projected eigensolve, and finite-dimensional arithmetic or orthogonalization
operation returns its value or its prescribed failure status after finitely
many operations. Then the execution returns one of the statuses listed by its
procedure after finitely many operations. In particular, the Arnoldi
procedure performs at most $N_{\max}$ restarts and at most $N_{\max}+1$
Arnoldi cycles, and the LOBPCG procedure performs at most $N_{\max}$ updates.
lem-generalized-ritz-values-monotone-und:
## Statement

Let $A=A^*\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ and $B=B^*>0$. Write the generalized
eigenvalues of $(A,B)$ in increasing order
$\lambda_1\le\cdots\le\lambda_n$. For a subspace $S$ with a full-column-rank
$B$-orthonormal basis matrix $Q_S$, let
$\theta_1(S)\le\cdots\le\theta_{\dim S}(S)$ be the eigenvalues of
$Q_S^*AQ_S$. These values are independent of the chosen $B$-orthonormal basis.
Then, for $1\le j\le\dim S$,
$$\lambda_j\le\theta_j(S).$$
If $S\subseteq T$ and $j\le\dim S$, then
$$\theta_j(T)\le\theta_j(S).$$
lem-block-principal-angle-squared-ritz-e:
## Statement

Let $A=A^*\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, $B=B^*>0$, and
$\lambda_1\le\cdots\le\lambda_n$ be the generalized eigenvalues of $(A,B)$.
Fix $1\le q<n$ with the strict gap $\lambda_q<\lambda_{q+1}$ and let
$U=\operatorname{span}\{u_1,\ldots,u_q\}$ be the corresponding sum of the
first $q$ eigenspaces, with $(u_i)$ $B$-orthonormal. For a $q$-dimensional
trial subspace $S$ with $B$-orthonormal basis $Q$, define
$$P_Ux=\sum_{i=1}^q u_i(u_i^*Bx),\qquad \sin\vartheta=\sup_{\substack{x\in S\\\|x\|_B=1}}\|(I-P_U)x\|_B.$$
Let $\theta_1(S)\le\cdots\le\theta_q(S)$ be the generalized Ritz values
from [[lem-generalized-ritz-values-monotone-under-nested-subspaces]]. Then
$$\lambda_j\le\theta_j(S)\quad(1\le j\le q),\qquad \theta_q(S)\le\lambda_q+(\lambda_n-\lambda_q)\sin^2\vartheta.$$
The strict gap identifies $U$ uniquely; the estimate is a subspace enclosure,
not an iteration convergence rate.
thm-lobpcg-selected-ritz-values-do-not-i:
## Statement

Let $A=A^*$ and $B=B^*>0$. Suppose one successful update of
[[alg-block-lobpcg-with-rank-loss-status]] starts from a $q$-dimensional
$B$-orthonormal block $X_k$ with selected Ritz values
$\theta_1(X_k)\le\cdots\le\theta_q(X_k)$. The update forms a trial space
$S_k=\operatorname{span}(X_k,W_k,D_k)$, retains the old block, and selects the
$q$ smallest generalized Ritz values on $S_k$. Then
$$\theta_j(X_{k+1})\le\theta_j(X_k)\qquad(1\le j\le q).$$
This assertion applies only to an update that reaches the Rayleigh-Ritz step;
the algorithm's `rank-loss` and `budget-exhausted` exits make no update claim.
alg-shift-invert-and-harmonic-ritz-extra:
## Definition

Let $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, $n\ge1$, choose a shift
$\sigma\in\mathbb C$, and put $M=A-\sigma I$. This procedure returns candidate
values and their residual data; it asserts no convergence or forward-error
bound. Its branch statuses are `available`, `arnoldi-breakdown`,
`linear-solve-unavailable`, `zero-transformed-Ritz-value`,
`infinite-harmonic-value`, `projected-pencil-unresolved`,
`qz-budget-exhausted`, and `qz-certificate-inconclusive`.

**Shift-invert branch.** This branch requires $M$ to be invertible, equivalently
that $\sigma$ is not an eigenvalue of $A$ by
[[prop-eigenvalue-iff-shift-is-not-invertible]]. Its inputs also include a
nonzero starting vector $v$, an integer Arnoldi dimension $1\le m\le n$, a
residual tolerance $\tau\ge0$, and a solve routine. Normalize
$v_1=v/\|v\|_2$. For $j=1,\ldots,m$, request either the exact solution
$y_j=M^{-1}v_j$ or a computed vector $y_j$ together with its actual equation
residual $s_j=My_j-v_j$. If a requested solve is unavailable, return
`linear-solve-unavailable` with the residuals already recorded. Set $w=y_j$.
For $i=1,\ldots,j$, compute $h_{ij}=\langle w,v_i\rangle$ and replace
$w\gets w-h_{ij}v_i$. Repeat this pass once, adding each second-pass
coefficient to the corresponding $h_{ij}$. Set $h_{j+1,j}=\|w\|_2$. If this
norm is zero, set the current dimension to $k=j$ and stop with status
`arnoldi-breakdown`; otherwise set $v_{j+1}=w/h_{j+1,j}$. After $m$ columns,
set $k=m$ and stop with status `available`.
When every solve is exact, this is Arnoldi applied to $M^{-1}$. When any solve
is inexact, the projected matrix is only the one produced from the computed
vectors; the procedure makes no exact-Arnoldi or convergence claim for that
branch.

Compute the Ritz pairs $(\theta,z)$ of the current $k\times k$ matrix $H$ as
in [[def-ritz-values-and-ritz-vectors-from-arnoldi]], normalize $z$ to unit
norm, and lift $u=V_kz$. For each $\theta\ne0$, report the transformed candidate
$\lambda=\sigma+1/\theta$, the lifted vector $u$, and the directly computed
original residual $r_A=Au-\lambda u$. Mark this candidate accepted exactly
when $\|r_A\|_2\le\tau$. If $\theta=0$, assign no finite inverse map and mark
that candidate `zero-transformed-Ritz-value`. To record the solve-error
transfer for a candidate with $\theta\ne0$, request one additional solve
$My=u$; if it is available, store $s_0=My-u$ and $r_T=y-\theta u$ alongside
the directly computed residual $r_A$.
If this additional solve is unavailable, return
`linear-solve-unavailable` with the candidate and accumulated ledger.

**Harmonic Ritz branch.** This branch takes a full-column-rank trial basis
$U\in\mathbb C^{n\times k}$, $k\ge1$; it does not require $M$ to be
invertible. Form $W=MU$ and
$$G=W^*W=U^*M^*MU,\qquad C=W^*U=U^*M^*U.$$
Compute an exact column-pivoted QR of $W$ as in
[[def-full-reduced-and-column-pivoted-computational-qr-factorisations]] and let
$r_W$ be its exact rank. If $r_W<k$, choose $z\ne0$ with $Wz=0$. Then
$z^*G=(Wz)^*W=0$ and $z^*C=(Wz)^*U=0$. Thus the nonzero row
$z^*$ annihilates $G-\eta C$ for every $\eta$; if this matrix were invertible,
right multiplication by its inverse would force $z^*=0$, a contradiction.
Hence $G-\eta C$ is singular for every $\eta$; return
`projected-pencil-unresolved`. If $W$ has full column rank, then
$z^*Gz=\|Wz\|_2^2>0$ for every $z\ne0$. Thus $G$ is positive definite and
the pencil $G-\eta C$ is regular in the convention of
[[def-regular-generalized-eigenvalue-pencil]], since
$\det(G-0C)=\det G\ne0$.

Supply a finite QZ sweep budget $N\ge0$ and tolerance $\tau_{QZ}\ge0$, and run
[[alg-finite-budget-qz-iteration-with-deflation-and-residual]] on $(G,C)$.
Compute $G,C$ exactly in the mathematical procedure; a finite implementation
must include their formation errors in the perturbation ledger or return
`qz-certificate-inconclusive`. On `qz-computed`, require its exact-factor and
local-update certificates;
[[prop-finite-budget-qz-iteration-terminates-and-preserves-pencil-equivalence]]
then records equivalence to a perturbed projected pencil. For each diagonal
index $i$, set $\alpha_i=S_{ii}$ and $\beta_i=T_{ii}$. If
$(\alpha_i,\beta_i)=(0,0)$, return `projected-pencil-unresolved`; if
$\beta_i\ne0$, report the computed harmonic Ritz value
$\lambda_i=\sigma+\alpha_i/\beta_i$; if $\beta_i=0$, mark that candidate
`infinite-harmonic-value`. These are values of the computed perturbed
pencil, with the QZ residual and perturbation ledger retained; no exact-root,
eigenvector, or forward-error claim is made. Map a QZ `budget-exhausted` status
to `qz-budget-exhausted`; map a QZ `certificate-inconclusive` or `range-failure`
to `qz-certificate-inconclusive`; map `singular-pencil-suspected` to
`projected-pencil-unresolved`.
thm-finite-budget-shift-invert-and-harmo:
## Statement

Consider a valid shift-invert or harmonic-extraction execution of
[[alg-shift-invert-and-harmonic-ritz-extraction]]. Assume each invoked solve,
projected eigensolve, finite-dimensional arithmetic or orthogonalization
operation returns its value or prescribed failure status after finitely
many operations. On the harmonic branch, also assume the finite-budget QZ
run satisfies the operationwise arithmetic hypotheses of
[[prop-finite-budget-qz-iteration-terminates-and-preserves-pencil-equivalence]].
Then the execution returns one of the statuses listed by the algorithm after
finitely many operations.
thm-shift-invert-map-and-inexact-solve-r:
## Statement

Let $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, $\sigma\in\mathbb C$, and
$M=A-\sigma I$ be invertible. Then a nonzero vector $u$ is an eigenvector of
$A$ with eigenvalue $\lambda$ if and only if it is an eigenvector of
$M^{-1}$ with eigenvalue $\theta=(\lambda-\sigma)^{-1}$. In particular,
$\lambda=\sigma+1/\theta$ and $\theta\ne0$.

For any nonzero candidate $u$, any $\theta\ne0$, and any computed vector $y$
with solve residual $s_0=My-u$, define the transformed residual
$r_T=y-\theta u$ and $\lambda=\sigma+1/\theta$. Then
$$ (A-\lambda I)u=\theta^{-1}(s_0-Mr_T), $$
and consequently
$$\|(A-\lambda I)u\|_2\le\frac{\|s_0\|_2+\|Mr_T\|_2}{|\theta|}.$$
